observation_summary: The BigFraction class fails to correctly compute doubleValue() and floatValue() for large BigInteger numerators and denominators because it directly converts them to double/float, which results in NaN or Infinity due to overflow, even when the ratio is representable.
hypothesis: The BigFraction.doubleValue() and floatValue() methods are implemented by directly dividing the results of BigInteger.doubleValue() and BigInteger.floatValue(). When the BigInteger values are extremely large (exceeding the range of double/float), these methods return Infinity or NaN, even if the ratio of the two numbers is within the representable range. The fix requires implementing a scaling mechanism (shifting bits) to bring the numerator and denominator into the representable range before division.
prediction: The implementation of BigFraction.doubleValue() and floatValue() will show a simple division of the BigInteger values converted to double/float, lacking any logic to handle overflow or scaling.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and stack trace confirm that the failure occurs during the conversion of large BigIntegers to double/float. The fix involves adding a scaling algorithm to handle these large values, which is a procedural change to the method's logic.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a failure to correctly compute a value due to an inadequate computational strategy (direct conversion) for large inputs. This is a classic Algorithm/Method defect as it requires a change to the procedure to handle the range constraints of the target types.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a check (if NaN), the core issue is the lack of a robust algorithm to compute the value when the direct conversion fails.
